summary: A single-session airline+retail concierge run for Maya (Lin) Chen, entirely threaded by back-references to reservation C4C633. The arc: look up C4C633 with flight status (T1), rename a passenger Maya Chen→Maya Lin Chen (T2), formally process a no-op flight update (T3), add a paid checked bag (T4), pull the second booking EC4C1C and compare it to C4C633 (T5), text Jordan Kim with a booking reminder (T6), then a retail detour — electronics search + return-policy review (T7) and processing Jordan Lee's clothing return (T8) — before a C4C633 recap (T9) and session summary (T10). The recall-heaviest turns are T5 (EC4C1C-vs-C4C633 comparison) and T9/T10 (full recaps). All four probe turns (T2, T3, T6, T10) are answered from working memory with no re-retrieval, and the agent routes around FlightDB.load() validation errors by going straight to SQL on every write. Recall is strong (24/27 credited); quality is high — the one subtlety is T3, where the ‘flight update’ is a genuine no-op the agent correctly recognizes and processes without inventing a fare difference.

**Return windows by category:**
| Category | Window |
|---|---|
| Electronics | **15 days** |
| Clothing | **30 days** |
| Kitchen | 30 days |
| Accessories | 30 days |

**Window extensions:**
- Gold/Platinum members: +15 days
- Prime shipping members: +15 additional days
- Seasonal (Nov/Dec orders): extended through January 31 of the following year
**Store credit grace period:** Up to 15 days past the return window — store credit refund only.
**Eligibility exceptions:** Defective, wrong item, or damaged-in-transit items have no window restriction.

### 3. Your Shirt Return — Which Window Applies?
A shirt is **clothing**, so it falls under the **30-day clothing return window** — not the shorter 15-day electronics window. The electronics window only applies to products in the electronics category. Your shirt return gets the full 30 days from the delivery/purchase date (plus any membership or Prime extensions you may qualify for).
